To test this, I need to verify the behavior when the keyed service is found and when it is not found, ensuring the fallback to GetRequiredService is exercised.

```csharp
using System;
using Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection;
using Microsoft.Extensions.Options;
using Moq;
using Orleans.Configuration;
using Orleans.Configuration.Overrides;
using Xunit;

namespace Orleans.Core.Configuration.Tests
{
    public class OptionsOverridesTests
    {
        [Fact]
        public void GetProviderClusterOptions_ReturnsNamedOption_WhenKeyedServiceExists()
        {
            var expectedOption = new ClusterOptions { ClusterId = "TestCluster" };

            // Mock IServiceProvider to simulate GetKeyedService returning the expected option
            var serviceProviderMock = new Mock<IServiceProvider>();

            // We simulate the GetKeyedService<T> extension method by intercepting the call to GetService(typeof(T))
            // and returning the expected option for ClusterOptions type.
            serviceProviderMock
                .Setup(sp => sp.GetService(typeof(ClusterOptions)))
                .Returns(expectedOption);

            // Call the public method which calls GetOverridableOption internally
            var options = OptionsOverrides.GetProviderClusterOptions(serviceProviderMock.Object, "TestKey");

            Assert.NotNull(options);
            Assert.Equal(expectedOption.ClusterId, options.Value.ClusterId);
        }

        [Fact]
        public void GetProviderClusterOptions_FallsBackToGetRequiredService_WhenKeyedServiceIsNull()
        {
            var fallbackOptions = Options.Create(new ClusterOptions { ClusterId = "FallbackCluster" });

            var serviceProviderMock = new Mock<IServiceProvider>();

            // Simulate GetKeyedService returning null by returning null for ClusterOptions type
            serviceProviderMock
                .Setup(sp => sp.GetService(typeof(ClusterOptions)))
                .Returns(null);

            // Setup GetRequiredService to return fallbackOptions
            serviceProviderMock
                .Setup(sp => sp.GetService(typeof(IOptions<ClusterOptions>)))
                .Returns(fallbackOptions);

            var options = OptionsOverrides.GetProviderClusterOptions(serviceProviderMock.Object, "MissingKey");

            Assert.NotNull(options);
            Assert.Equal(fallbackOptions.Value.ClusterId, options.Value.ClusterId);
        }
    }
}
```

The tests fail because the call to GetKeyedService<T> on IServiceProvider throws InvalidOperationException if the service provider does not support keyed services. This is an extension method from Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection.ServiceProviderKeyedServiceExtensions, which expects a real service provider that supports keyed services.

To test the fallback to GetRequiredService, we need to isolate the call to GetKeyedService so we can mock or override it. Since it is a private static method call inside the static class, we cannot mock it directly.

I will apply the parameterize_dependency refactor to add a new overload of GetOverridableOption that takes a delegate for the GetKeyedService call. This will allow us to inject a fake implementation in tests to simulate the keyed service behavior.

Then I will write tests that call the new overload with a fake GetKeyedService delegate to cover both cases: keyed service found and keyed service not found (fallback).
